newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean LG-Caltex delays feeding crude to new CDU.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean LG-Caltex delays feeding crude to new CDU.

text.p: South Korea's LG-Caltex Oil Corp, a unit of LG Group delayed feeding crude oil to its new crude distillation unit (CDU) after finding a defect in the unit's column, a senior company official said on Monday.
LG-Caltex had previously scheduled to feed the crude on November 16.
"We had to postpone the feed-in date because we have found a defect in the topper's column and need time to fix it," the official at the LG-Caltex's refinery in Yeochon told Reuters.
The delay is also expected to force the company to put off full production at the unit, which was originally scheduled to start on November 23, he said.
"It's hard to tell at the moment when we can start running the unit. We need some time to assess the problem," he said.
The new CDU has been mechanically completed and it was currently going through final checks for possible leaks and pressure.
LG-Caltex will rely on light and sweet crude oil as the feed for the 220,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) unit, he said.
The unit will boost LG-Caltex's licensed crude processing capacity to 600,000 bpd to become the nation's second largest refiner.
South Korea currently has a refining capability of 2.22 million bpd of crude.
LG-Caltex is a joint venture between LG Group and Caltex Petroleum Corp, itself a joint venture between U.S. oil giants Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
